dataset.name: Synthetic demonstration production (SYN-A, SYN-B, SYN-C)
dataset.banner: SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA - not MOIL operational records. Forecasts and risk bands illustrate the workflow only.

provenance.label: SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA
provenance.description: Deterministic daily production records for fictional mines SYN-A, SYN-B and SYN-C. Planned and actual tonnes, equipment downtime, weather and blasting delays, and rainfall are generated from simple, documented rules.
provenance.licence: Not applicable (synthetic data generated for this demonstration).
limitations: Not MOIL operational data and not calibrated to any real mine.
Relationships between delays and output are designed into the generator; associations found in this dataset describe the generator, not real operations.
Rainfall is synthetic here. Enrich the dataset with a public rainfall series to replace it.

expected.interval_basis: empirical 10th-90th percentile of 204 overlapping 30-day backtest windows

shortfall_probability.period_basis: Share of backtest windows of the same length in which the realised gap was below plan, given the forecast net gap. Empirical, not a calibrated model output.
shortfall_probability.daily_definition: Material shortfall day: actual below 95% of planned tonnes.

band.label: High
band.rule: HIGH when the expected net gap to plan is at or below -5%; MEDIUM when it is at or below -2%; otherwise LOW. Thresholds are policy choices and are not learned from data.

classification_check.text: AUC 0.84 and Brier skill +11.9% against a base-rate forecast on the backtest.

model_check.regression_text: The gradient boosting model has lower MAE than the best baseline, and the 95% interval for the difference excludes zero on this backtest.

limitations: Net gap is forecast plan minus forecast output over the horizon. Negative means shortfall.
Interval and period probability are empirical from backtest residuals, not a calibrated predictive distribution.
Future operational inputs (downtime, weather, blasting, rainfall) are scenario assumptions, so the forecast is conditional on them.
